text:
### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, the six activities A20, A22, A23, A24, A25 and A26 — each occurring in essentially every trace in both windows — were executed in varying orders: A20 and A26, and A22 and A24, had no fixed order (each order about 49–50 in 100 traces), A24 usually preceded A20 (about 73 in 100) and A23 (about 88 in 100), and A26 usually preceded A23 (about 70 in 100). In the later window a single fixed order dominates: A20 precedes A24 in about 99 in 100 traces, A22 precedes A24 in about 99, A23 precedes A24 in about 97, A20 precedes A25 in about 99 and A26 in about 98, and A23 precedes A25 in about 97 and A26 in about 96. [REL014, REL015, REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL021]

- Successors concentrated accordingly in the later window: A31 now leads to A22 in about 99 in 100 of its outgoing transitions (before, split about 50/50 between A24 and A22), A22 to A20 in about 98 (before about 56), A20 to A23 in about 99 (before about 62), A23 to A24 in about 98 (before, A32 took about 48), A24 to A26 in about 99 (before about 55), A26 to A25 in about 99 (before about 65) and A25 to A32 in about 90 (before about 42) — consistent with one chain, roughly A31 → A22 → A20 → A23 → A24 → A26 → A25 → A32. [DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, DIR010, DIR011, DIR012, DIR013]

- Positions shifted slightly in the same direction: A20, A22 and A23 now appear a little earlier within traces (median shifts of roughly 0.03–0.07 in event-position units) and A24 and A26 a little later (roughly 0.03–0.06); these are event positions, not clock times. [POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006]

- A08 was executed far less often: about 72 in 100 traces earlier versus about 29 in 100 later (mean occurrences per trace 0.75 versus about 0.32); when present, it appears later and more variably within the trace (mean relative position about 0.24 versus 0.41), and its transitions to A16 fell from about 90% to about 39% of its outgoing transitions, spreading over A48 (about 16%), A15 (about 15%) and others. Thirteen pair items show its co-occurrence with A14, A15, A16, A20, A22, A23, A24, A25, A26, A31, A32, A47 and A48 falling in lockstep from 72 to 29 in 100 traces — one participation change seen from many angles, not independent findings. [OCC001, DIR003, POS001, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013]

- A15 was rerouted and A10 occurred more often: after A15, transitions to A16 rose from about 58% to about 87% while those to A08 fell from about 42% to about 7%; A10 now appears in about 22 in 100 traces versus about 8 in 100, with a changed successor mix (A48 about 31% of its outgoing transitions; A30 down from about 21% to about 2%, on only 14 versus 49 transitions). A02 and A04 also show redistributed successors, but on few observations (about 15–19 transitions before, 37–40 after). [DIR006, OCC002, DIR004, DIR001, DIR002]

- Elsewhere behaviour was stable: the dominant edges A14 → A15, A45 → A46 and A47 → A48 remained dominant in both windows with only small share shifts. [DIR005, DIR014, DIR015]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the ordering constraints between A20, A22, A23, A24, A25 and A26 were tightened: in the earlier window these activities, which always occurred together, were executed in varying orders with several pairs unordered or commonly reversed and A23 most often followed by A32, while in the later window they follow one fixed sequence, approximately A31 → A22 → A20 → A23 → A24 → A26 → A25 → A32. The support is direct and consistent: all eight observed activity pairs moved from mixed or reversed orders to the same fixed order while co-occurrence stayed at 100 in 100 traces in both windows, so this is a change in ordering constraints rather than a change in which activities run together; the successor profiles of A31, A22, A20, A23, A24, A26 and A25 agree with the same chain; and the screening statistics (44 qualifying items against about 0.62 expected if nothing had changed) make sampling variation implausible as an account of the pattern as a whole. [REL014, REL015, REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL021, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, DIR010, DIR011, DIR012, DIR013]

Limitations: the fixed sequence is reconstructed from pairwise orders and per-successor shares in two 200-trace windows rather than observed as complete end-to-end variants, so a per-case tightening of the order cannot be distinguished from a shift in the mix of execution variants carrying different orders; a connection with the concurrent rerouting around A08 and A15 also cannot be ruled out. [OCC001, DIR006, REL016, REL019]

Other differences: A08 was skipped far more often in the later window (about 72 in 100 traces before versus about 29 in 100, appearing later within traces when present), A10 was executed more often (about 8 versus about 22 in 100 traces) with a changed successor mix, and A02 and A04 show weakly supported successor redistributions; these participation and routing changes are not part of the ordering hypothesis above. [OCC001, OCC002, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, POS001]
